name: Hydrochloric acid

molar_mass_g_mol.source: sum of abridged standard atomic weights in data/elements/elements.json

appearance: Clear, colourless solution; concentrated acid fumes in moist air.

density_g_cm3.source: General-chemistry reference values recalled from memory; check a supplier data sheet or handbook before teaching use.

solubility_in_water.note: Hydrogen chloride gas is very soluble in water. The density is for concentrated (about 37 %) acid.

hazards.summary: Concentrated acid burns skin and eyes and its fumes irritate the lungs. Dilute solutions are mildly irritating.
hazards.source: General-chemistry reference values recalled from memory; check a supplier data sheet or handbook before teaching use.

storage: Closed, labelled container, away from bases and metals.

reactions.note: Reacts with bases to give a salt and water, releasing heat.
Reacts with many metals (hydrogen) and carbonates (carbon dioxide).

educational_notes: A strong acid: in water every molecule gives up its hydrogen ion, so the pH of 0.1 mol/L acid is about 1.
